parsed.draft_response:
Thanks for flagging this—given the possibility of cross-tenant access via forwarded report links, we’ll treat this as a high-priority security review and handle it as confidential.

At this point, we haven’t validated exfiltration, so the first goal is to confirm what the forwarded link can actually access (e.g., whether the other workspace can view and/or download report content) and whether any audit evidence shows access attempts.

To help our security team investigate quickly, please reply with:
1) Exact report/link details: product/workspace context, report type, and how the link was shared (share settings, whether it’s “public,” “authenticated,” “shared link,” etc.).
2) What “visible” means in your observation: did the other workspace only see the link in UI, or were they able to open it and view/download data?
3) Affected tenants/workspaces (IDs or names) and approximate timestamps.
4) Whether you can provide any relevant audit/log event references (request IDs, user IDs, timestamps, and outcomes).
5) Whether the issue is reproducible and under what conditions (any roles/permissions, link expiration, reliability).

In parallel, please avoid circulating the URL further (including in tickets/chats beyond your organization) and, if feasible, consider temporarily disabling/deleting the shared link(s) involved to reduce any potential exposure while we investigate.

We’ve escalated this to our security team for human review. Once we have the details above, we’ll follow up on findings and the recommended remediation steps.
promised_actions: Escalate the report to the security team for human review
Request specific additional details needed to confirm whether cross-tenant access occurred and what the link permits
safety_notes: Do not confirm cross-tenant access/exfiltration without evidence.
Ask for minimal necessary information to validate access capability and audit evidence.
Avoid promising a fix, refund, SLA, or final security/legal conclusion.

parsed.customer_impact: Potential unauthorized cross-tenant access to report data if forwarded links allow other workspaces to view/download content, representing a security risk; actual exfiltration has not been confirmed.
grounded_facts: A report link created by one user may be visible to another workspace if the URL is forwarded.
The reporter has not confirmed data exfiltration.
The observed behavior appears to be cross-tenant access.
The ticket requests confidential handling and advice on next steps.
The issue is classified as security with high urgency and needs human security review.
missing_information: Whether any access was actually performed by the other workspace (proof of exposure vs. mere URL visibility).
Whether the shared URL allows viewing/download of sensitive report data or only reveals link metadata.
Examples of the affected tenants/workspaces and timestamps when the behavior occurred.
Exact product/service name, report/link type, and sharing settings involved.
Whether this occurs reliably or only under specific conditions (e.g., role/permissions, user types, link expiration).
Whether logs/audit events exist showing cross-tenant access attempts and outcomes.
Impact assessment: how much data (if any) could be accessed and whether it includes personal or regulated data.
risk_signals: High-urgency security concern with apparent cross-tenant access behavior.
Potential for unauthorized disclosure of tenant report data via shared links.
Unconfirmed but concerning behavior where URL forwarding may bypass expected tenant boundaries.
parsed.summary: A user reported that a report URL shared by one user might be visible in another workspace if the URL is forwarded, suggesting possible cross-tenant data exposure, and requested confidential next steps despite no confirmed data exfiltration.
